number.why: The served outcome specifies intention-to-treat. Its rivaroxaban-versus-warfarin HR is 0.88 with 95% CI 0.74 to 1.03 for stroke or systemic embolism. The ruling correctly identifies the conflicting per-protocol row label; correcting that label preserves the intended ITT number. The precise ITT follow-up time remains unestablished, as the ruling acknowledges.

quotes.span: The per-protocol, as-treated primary analysis was designed to determine whether rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin for the primary end point of stroke or systemic embolism.

In the intention-to-treat analysis, the primary end point occurred in 269 patients in the rivaroxaban group (2.1% per year) and in 306 patients in the warfarin group (2.4% per year) (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.03; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.12 for superiority).

In the primary analysis, the primary end point occurred in 188 patients in the rivaroxaban group (1.7% per year) and in 241 in the warfarin group (2.2% per year) (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority).

entry.why: The packet establishes adult eligibility and nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, with a randomized direct comparison of an oral factor Xa inhibitor against warfarin. Increased stroke risk narrows the eligible population within the question's scope.

quotes.span: ELIGIBILITY AGE/SEX: minimum age 18 Years | maximum age None | sex ALL
Rivaroxaban, an oral factor Xa inhibitor, may provide more consistent and predictable anticoagulation than warfarin.

In a double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 14,264 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation who were at increased risk for stroke to receive either rivaroxaban (at a daily dose of 20 mg) or dose-adjusted warfarin.

missed: No additional finding changes either ruling. Numerical confirmation remains conditional on correcting the analysis-set label to intention-to-treat; it does not establish the served 'trial end' timepoint.
